metas.name: Master and Commander: The Far Side of the World
metas.description: Captures a ship as a complete working system. During the Napoleonic Wars a British frigate hunts a French ship around South America — seamanship, weather and hierarchy, and a captain whose naturalist friend would rather be cataloguing species in the Galápagos.

metas.name: Sorcerer
metas.description: Captures pure physical tension. Four fugitives in South America take the only job out — hauling unstable nitroglycerin in old trucks through jungle — centred on getting a truck across a rotting rope bridge in a storm, in real time.

metas.name: Mad Max: Fury Road
metas.description: Captures momentum as a physical state. Almost no dialogue, one chase out and one chase back — speed, heat and desperation, with a war-rig as a whole society in miniature.

metas.name: Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse
metas.director: Bob Persichetti, Peter Ramsey, Rodney Rothman
metas.description: Captures what a comic book actually feels like to read, in motion. Also a genuinely good story about a kid learning that anyone can wear the mask, by failing at it a lot.

metas.name: Barry Lyndon
metas.description: Captures a rise and fall narrated like fate already happened. An Irish opportunist climbs 18th-century society through duels, war and marriage, shot like paintings, with a narrator who keeps telling you the ending early.

metas.name: Lawrence of Arabia
metas.description: Captures a man inventing himself at desert scale. Nearly four hours: the landscape is a character, and so is the gap between the legend being built and the person inside it.

metas.name: Thelma & Louise
metas.description: Captures escape becoming irreversible, and friendship becoming absolute. A weekend trip, a parking lot, a gun — then two women driving west, getting freer and more cornered in the same scenes.

metas.name: Apollo 13
metas.description: Captures competence under constraint. An explosion in space, and the film becomes people in rooms with slide rules solving the next physical problem before the air runs out — the opposite of lone-hero cinema.

metas.name: Princess Mononoke
metas.description: Captures an ecological war with no pure side. Iron Town needs the forest cut to survive; the forest gods need the humans gone; a prince cursed by a dying god tries to see with unclouded eyes.

metas.name: Paddington 2
metas.description: Captures decency as something contagious. A bear framed for stealing the pop-up book he wanted to buy his aunt, sent to prison — and the prison improves because he is in it.

metas.name: Atanarjuat: The Fast Runner
metas.description: Captures an Inuit oral epic told by the community it belongs to. Made in Igloolik, in Inuktitut, with a largely Inuit cast and crew: a rivalry, a murder, and a naked run across the ice told for centuries.
